slide2:

Keep the white background, illustrated woman, friendly amber robot, purple documents, large navy text, landscape 16:9 and slide number 2. Make the whole result a clean, readable presentation slide.

Agent → Human: "Proposed rules + contrasting cases"
Human → Agent: "Judgments, preferences, exceptions"
Large unlabeled corpus → Agent: "Examples, boundaries, surprises"
Agent → large unlabeled corpus: "Inspect cases + test rules"

Replace the current two bottom output cards and their arrows with the SAME three-stage scaling pipeline used by use case 2:
Left document artifact "STRUCTURED GUIDELINE", caption "Human-approved rules and exceptions"
Middle three blue chips "EXECUTOR MODELS", caption "Test one guideline across models"
Right clean labeled-document stack "LARGE-SCALE LABELING", caption "Audited labeled corpus"

Connect the right-side LARGE UNLABELED CORPUS downward into LARGE-SCALE LABELING, explicitly supplying its items.
Remove the previous separate Accepted labeled data card and the earlier dangling branches.

Small footnote: "Human review or an explicit audit policy governs acceptance".
Keep clear whitespace and readable labels; do not shrink the text into a dense diagram.
slide3:
Revise slide 3 (image 1 is the edit target). Image 2 is the UPDATED use case 1 slide and is the style/layout reference: use the same lower scaling pipeline and the same large UNLABELED corpus on the RIGHT. Landscape 16:9, white background, clear navy typography, same illustrated characters and colors, page number 3.

Title: "Use case 2: an existing labeled corpus"
Subtitle: "Recover a standard from existing labels, then apply it to new items"

Crucial top-row layout:
LEFT: an unmistakable small stack of documents with visible old label tags and a few question marks, headed "LABELED CORPUS", caption "Existing labels + optional guideline". This is the starting evidence, NOT the new items to label.
CENTER: friendly amber AGENT, caption "Infers rules and groups issues".
RIGHT: much larger purple stack headed "LARGE UNLABELED CORPUS", caption "New items and edge cases". This is a SEPARATE corpus, just like use case 1.
The old slide's large woman on the left is replaced by the labeled-document stack. Retain the HUMAN as a smaller distinct reviewer icon beside or beneath the left source stack, with a readable caption "Human reviewer: confirm, revise or defer". No thought bubble for this reviewer. Do not let the reviewer replace the labeled corpus as the primary left entity.

Connect left labeled corpus → agent with "Patterns in existing labels".
Connect agent → left review area with "Candidate rules + issue groups".
Show that human review, not existing labels alone, confirms the standard. A brief note is sufficient: "Flags need human judgment".
On the right connect large unlabeled corpus → agent with "New cases and boundaries", and agent → large unlabeled corpus with "Inspect cases + test rules".

Bottom pipeline must match updated slide 2:
"STRUCTURED GUIDELINE" / "Human-approved rules and exceptions"
→ "EXECUTOR MODELS" / "Test one guideline across models"
→ "LARGE-SCALE LABELING" / "Audited labeled corpus"
The orange agent output must lead to STRUCTURED GUIDELINE, labeled "Record the accepted standard".
A blue loop from executor models back to structured guideline says "Refine wording, preserve meaning".
The right LARGE UNLABELED CORPUS connects downward into LARGE-SCALE LABELING, labeled "Supply items for labeling".
Bottom takeaway: "Different starting evidence, the same path to scale"
Small footer: "Human review or an explicit audit policy governs acceptance".
Avoid crowding: shorten labels where needed, keep text large. Preserve scientific meaning. Existing labeled data and the large unlabeled target corpus must be visibly different entities at opposite sides.
